activity.notes: Micanopy was recognized as the Seminoles' head or principal chief and was a central political figure in resistance to removal and the Second Seminole War. Seminole political authority was decentralized rather than a centralized monarchy, so 'Principal Chief' is retained rather than styling him king. Secondary accounts vary between an earlier hereditary succession date and the conventional c.1825 emergence as principal chief; ATLAS therefore marks the start approximate and ends the Activity with his death in 1849.

sources.title: Seminole Leaders — Florida Department of State
sources.citation_text: Florida's Department of State identifies Micanopy as Head Chief and one of the most important Seminole chiefs, noting his resistance to removal.

sources.title: American State Papers — Capitulation of the Seminole nation
sources.citation_text: The 1837 U.S. government record explicitly describes Micanopy as the principal chief of the Seminole nation.

sources.title: Micanopy, a Seminole chief — Florida Memory
sources.citation_text: Florida Memory identifies Micanopy as Head Chief or Governor and describes his role in uniting the Seminoles in the early nineteenth century.
